turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with columns: compound_id (e.g., Imatinib, Dasatinib, Nilotinib, Ponatinib), CLint_uL_per_min_mg (microsomal intrinsic clearance), molecular_weight
Key steps:

PKNCA + well-stirred/parallel-tube model → scales CLint_microsomal using MPPGL (microsomal protein per gram liver) & liver weight assumptions → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg)
Extraction ratio calculator → ER = CLh / Qh (hepatic blood flow ~20.7 mL/min/kg) → classifies each TKI as low/intermediate/high extraction


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg per compound, both model predictions) + clearance_summary.json (extraction ratio, classification, model comparison)

Decision gate: Flag any compound with ER > 0.7 (high extraction) — these are highly susceptible to first-pass effect and hepatic blood flow changes, which is critical for oral BCR-ABL1 TKI dosing decisions.

turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — BCR-ABL1 TKI Panel — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance and extraction ratio for 4 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs with measured parameters — Dasatinib (CLint=220 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Bosutinib (CLint=60 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.03), Imatinib (CLint=25 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.04), Nilotinib (CLint=12 μL/min/mg, fu_plasma=0.01); model parameters: Qh=20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic=1.0
Key steps:

PKNCA well-stirred model → scales CLint_microsomal via MPPGL (45 mg/g) × liver weight (21.4 g/kg) → CLint_scaled (mL/min/kg) per compound
Well-stirred liver equation → CLh = (Qh × fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint_scaled) → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg) + extraction ratio (ER = CLh / Qh)


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg, CLint_scaled, ER per compound for both well-stirred and parallel-tube models) + clearance_summary.json (ER classification: low <0.3 / intermediate 0.3–0.7 / high >0.7, model comparison flags)

Decision gate: Flag compounds with ER > 0.7 (high extraction) as first-pass sensitive — for oral BCR-ABL1 TKIs this predicts high hepatic extraction and susceptibility to CYP3A4 inhibitor/inducer DDIs, requiring dose adjustment review.

turns.query: Run pocket detection and druggability assessment on BCR-ABL1 kinase structure PDB:1IEP. I need the top 10 binding pockets ranked by druggability score and volume. BCR-ABL1 is in DFG-out conformation; …
turns.responseText:
BCR-ABL1 Pocket Detection & Druggability Assessment (1IEP) — Detects and ranks all binding pockets on the BCR-ABL1 kinase DFG-out structure using fpocket, prioritizing the imatinib allosteric site by druggability score and volume.

Input: PDB ID 1IEP (BCR-ABL1 kinase, DFG-out conformation, imatinib-bound)
Key steps:

fpocket → fetch & validate 1IEP PDB coordinates, strip solvent/ligands, run full pocket detection across the DFG-out surface
fpocket scoring engine → compute druggability score (0–1), volume (ų), hydrophobicity, and α-sphere density per pocket
Ranking module → sort all detected pockets by druggability score + volume, output top 10 with residue-level annotations


Expected output: pocket_summary.csv (top 10 pockets ranked by druggability score & volume) + druggability_scores.json (full scoring metadata per pocket) + ranked HTML report with 3D pocket visualizations and residue contact maps

Decision gate: Prioritize pockets with fpocket druggability score ≥ 0.5 and volume ≥ 300 ų — the canonical imatinib DFG-out allosteric pocket on BCR-ABL1 (1IEP) is expected to rank #1 with a score > 0.7 and volume ~900 ų, confirming site suitability for lead optimization.

Pharmacophore Alignment → screens all 4 library compounds against the model, scores each by number of matched pharmacophoric features, and ranks hits above the min_features = 3 threshold

Decision gate: Compounds matching ≥ 3 pharmacophoric features advance; expect Gleevec-analog-1 and Ponatinib to pass (structurally similar to reference inhibitors), while Terfenadine and Acetaminophen are likely filtered out as non-ABL1-like scaffolds.

BCR-ABL1 Campaign Safety-Potency Ranking — Ingests dual-assay IC50 data for 15 compounds and produces a composite score ranking potency against BCR-ABL1 kinase alongside hERG cardiac safety.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 in nM + hERG_IC50 in µM, dated 2026-03-15)

Ranking Engine → sorts by composite score descending, appends risk tier (Green / Amber / Red) → ranked_compounds.csv + HTML report

WuXi column formatter → maps compound_id, SMILES, IC50_nM, hERG_IC50_uM, composite_score to WuXi AppTec submission schema + computes MW/LogP via RDKit
CSV export → generates wuxiapptec_submission.csv + metadata JSON with campaign provenance

Decision gate: Any compound with hERG IC50 ≤ 1 μM is automatically withheld from the export — the metadata JSON will log the reason. All 5 compounds must clear this threshold for a full 5-row submission file.
